facts.content: The patient has an intensely itchy, sore, red rash lasting 4 days and wants rapid relief.
facts.source_text: CC: Intensely pruritic, sore, red rash x4 days; wants rapid relief

facts.content: The rash is distributed on the chest, hands, and antecubital fossae, but not on the face.
facts.source_text: Distribution: Chest, hands, antecubital fossae; no face

facts.content: Severe itch causes poor sleep and impaired focus at work, and limits hiking.
facts.source_text: Severity/impact: Severe itch; poor sleep; impaired focus at work; limits hiking

facts.content: Skin features cracked areas without bleeding or discharge.
facts.source_text: Skin: Cracked areas; no bleeding or discharge

facts.content: No fever, bowels are okay, no cough or shortness of breath, and voiding is okay.
facts.source_text: ROS: No fever; bowels OK; no cough/SOB; voiding OK

facts.content: History of eczema and inactive past asthma.
Patient is not on any regular medication but tried OTC steroid cream and antihistamines without relief.
facts.source_text: Meds: None regular; tried OTC steroid cream (name unk) last night—no relief; tried OTC antihistamines—no relief

facts.content: Lives with flatmates and works as a project manager at a pharmaceutical company.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives with flatmates; works as project manager at a pharmaceutical company

facts.content: Non-smoker and consumes a few beers per week.
Eczema flare with severe pruritus on the chest, hands, and flexures; no systemic symptoms.
facts.source_text: 1) Eczema flare with severe pruritus—chest/hands/flexures; no systemic sx; no reported discharge/pus; OTC steroid and antihistamines ineffective

facts.content: Sleep disturbance is secondary to pruritus.
Prescribe a stronger topical corticosteroid than OTC.
facts.source_text: Topical corticosteroid Rx (stronger than OTC); apply as directed

facts.content: Use emollients during bath/shower and moisturize regularly for 7–10 days before evaluating the response.
facts.source_text: Emollients for bath/shower and regular moisturization; use consistently x7–10 days before judging response

facts.content: Prescribe Fexofenadine and consider OTC loratadine or Piriton for itch.
facts.source_text: Antihistamine: Fexofenadine Rx; may also try OTC loratadine or Piriton for itch

facts.content: Maintain a trigger diary to review and avoid potential irritants like soaps and clothing.
facts.source_text: Trigger diary; review/avoid potential irritants (soaps, shower gels, clothing)

facts.content: Follow-up next week if no improvement.
facts.source_text: FU next week if not improving
